headline: The research preprint site arXiv is limiting submitters to two papers a month as AI-written submissions surge, and a new study proposes a way to spot and repair low-quality AI-written papers.
score_reason: Real strain on science publishing, but the arXiv move was announced about a week earlier and the study figures are the authors' own.
importance_line: Researchers and journal editors face more low-value submissions, and the new detection method has only been tested by its own authors.
summary: Unite.AI reports that arXiv, the open preprint server, announced a limit of two submissions per month per submitter after receiving 40,363 submissions in September 2026, nearly double the September 2024 count, with moderators citing a rise in thin and AI-written papers. It also covers a Seoul National University and University of Minnesota benchmark, SciSlopBench, which picked out the AI-written paper in 85.9% of 390 human and AI pairs, a result from the authors' own tests.
notes: arXiv announcement described as 'last week' in the 4 Oct article, so lowered 5 to 4 as not new today. Benchmark figures are the authors' own.
